issue.title: Settings from .env are not picked up
issue.body:
I copied the example app and adjusted it. My .env contains:

    DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost/app
    PORT=9000

In the app I read the settings like this:

    config = Config.from_file('.env')
    db_url = config.get('database_url')
    port = config.get_int('port', 8000)

`config.get('database_url')` raises `KeyError: 'database_url'`, and the app starts on port 8000 instead of 9000, as if the PORT line wasn't there. If I copy the key names exactly as they appear in the file it works, but we use lower-case names everywhere else in our code.

confload 0.1.0, Python 3.10.

# confload

Load settings from dotenv-style files or environment variables.

See docs/usage.md once it exists.

commits.message: Document usage, key names and types

files.docs/usage.md:
# Usage

## Loading settings

    config = Config.from_file('.env')
    config.get('database_url')

Use `Config.from_file(path)` for a dotenv-style file or `Config.from_environ(prefix)` for environment variables. A `default` passed to `get` is returned when the key is missing.

## Key names

Key names are case-insensitive: `DATABASE_URL`, `database_url` and `Database_Url` all refer to the same setting, so you can use the style that fits your code.

## Types

`get_int` converts the value to an integer and raises `ValueError` when it is not a number.
files.README.md:
# confload

Load settings from dotenv-style files or environment variables.

See [docs/usage.md](docs/usage.md) for the full guide.

files.example/app.py:
from confload.config import Config

config = Config.from_file('example/.env')
db_url = config.get('DATABASE_URL')
port = config.get_int('PORT', 8000)
print(f'connecting to {db_url} on port {port}')

expected.cause: Keys are stored exactly as written in the file and looked up verbatim in Config.get, with no case normalisation anywhere, although docs/usage.md says key names are case-insensitive.

notes: Documentation (docs/usage.md) promises case-insensitive keys; code is case-sensitive. The example app only uses upper-case names so it hides the problem. Reporter does not name the docs.
